messages:
jordan: Hey team — Acme (tenant acme-477) is seeing a sharp p95 latency jump and intermittent 429s from their dedicated eu3 pool after we bumped autoscale. Started ~2026-06-10 14:02 UTC. Logs show repeated "RPC timeout" and header X-Request-Reason: throttled_kernel_busy.

maria: Can you drop tenant + pool + a quick sample trace link? I'll pull traces.

jordan: tenant=acme-477, pool=ded-eu3-74. Trace: https://console.redwood/instruments/trace/2105551234-xt
Here’s a minimal curl that reproduces the 429 quickly:
```
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"open-1-large","input":"ping"}' -i
```
Response headers include: `X-Request-Reason: throttled_kernel_busy` and body has 429.

opsbot: Incident INC-2026-0347 created and assigned to oncall-kevin.

kevin: Oncall here. Quick question: did customer run any large batch/finetune around 13:55-14:05? Those tend to cause sibling thrash.

jordan: Customer claims their finetune was targeted at another pool, but they did run a one-off evaluation at 13:59. Could be noisy neighbor on the same host.

sam: Can infra list node packing for ded-eu3-74? Run:
```
/opt/redwood/bin/node-inspect --pool ded-eu3-74 --format json | jq '.nodes[] | {id,allocations}'
```

kevin: I pulled prometheus: host node-147 shows SM_util spike to 95% at 14:01, NVLink peer bytes up, and KV cache hits drop (more misses). Correlated with tenant p95 going 70ms -> 1.2s. Suspect MIG sibling SM saturation or L3 thrash.

maria: Can you dump nvml/mig info from node-147?
```
python - <<'PY'
import pynvml
pynvml.nvmlInit()
h = pynvml.nvmlDeviceGetHandleByIndex(0)
print(pynvml.nvmlDeviceGetName(h))
for i in range(pynvml.nvmlDeviceGetMaxMigDeviceCount(h)):
  try:
    mg = pynvml.nvmlDeviceGetMigDeviceHandleByIndex(h, i)
    print(i, pynvml.nvmlDeviceGetUtilizationRates(mg))
  except:
    pass
PY
```

jordan: Pasted a trimmed nvml output from node-147: "MIG slice 0 util 98%, memory 88%, temp 78C". Also kernel logs show lots of "gpu context switch" messages.

kevin: Hypothesis: mixed MIG partitions on same physical host with a high-throughput consumer caused SM-level starvation for other slices -> long tail latency and throttles. Could be exacerbated by an autoscale bump that re-packed pods onto that node.

sam: Also see a few dmesg lines: "nvidia: unbounded page fault, migrating pages" — suggests memory churn/eviction. That plus KV cache misses will amplify token latency.

maria: Short repro plan:
1) Spin a stress container on node-147 that mimics small-batch high-req QPS (gpu micro-benchmark) to see p95 effect.
2) Run local inference against a small model pinned to a different slice on same node.
3) Capture nvml util and perf counters.

kevin: For quick mitigation I recommend draining node-147 from the pool and letting autoscaler rebalance: 
```
redwoodctl nodes drain node-147 --pool ded-eu3-74 --reason "noisy-neighbor triage"
```
Also temporarily bump per-tenant eviction threshold for acme-477.

maria: Added to runbook and posted a short command set to reproduce the 429 locally (use header X-Test-Mode):
```
for i in {1..200}; do 
  curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Test-Mode: noisy" -d '{"model":"open-1-small","input":"a"}' &
done; wait
```

acme-support: Thanks — we ran the test per your curl and saw the 429s disappear after you drained the node. What about billing/credits for the impact window?

kevin: We'll file a credit request for the outage window. Not billing while the customer's requests were throttled by our side. Filing SVC case and notifying finance.

jordan: Follow-ups captured:
- Drain node-147 and verify rebalance (done)
- Run stress repro (sam)
- Validate KV cache recovery and hits (maria)
- Patch autoscaler decider to consider node-level sm_util > 80% as a signal to avoid packing
- Eng-runtime to look for possible kernel driver edge-case on page migration

sam: Flagging eng-runtime and eng-ml for potential kernel/driver angle (tagging @eng-runtime @eng-ml). Also note kernel version on node-147 is 5.15.12 — might be relevant.

opsbot: Maintenance action queued: node-147 drained, expected rebalance in 3m.

acme-support: Confirmed latency returned to baseline ~2 minutes after drain. Will monitor for 24h and report.

kevin: I'll keep incident open until 24h stable. If reproducible we may enforce stronger isolation (dedicated slice placements) for high-SLA tenants.

maria: Nice triage everyone. I'll add a short KB entry: "Dedicated pool noisy neighbor: identify MIG SM saturation -> drain -> add autoscaler guardrails" with the exact commands used.

jordan: Closing notes: possible longer-term fixes: default anti-affinity for mixed compute profiles on same host, KV cache warmup heuristics, and autoscaler thresholds for per-node sm_util. :thumbsup:

acme-support: Appreciate the quick help — thank you!
